draft.title: The Civil War
card: The Civil War was fought in Russia from 1918 to 1921. The Reds were the Bolsheviks and their Red Army. They fought many groups that opposed Bolshevik rule.
a loose set of anti-Bolshevik forces, including army officers, monarchists and some liberals. They were united mainly by opposition to the Bolsheviks, and they had no single leader or plan.
Some foreign powers, including Britain, France, Japan and the United States, sent troops or supplies to the Whites. Their help was limited and did not win the war.

The Reds won by 1921. They held the central cities and railways, had one command and one aim, and could call on the Bolsheviks' wartime control of the economy to supply the army. The Whites were split and fought far apart.
draft.remember: The Reds won because they were united and held the centre. The Whites were divided.

a.q: Which was a main weakness of the Whites in the Civil War?
opts: They were united mainly by opposition to the Bolsheviks
They had no help from any foreign power
They held the central cities and railways
They fought under one command with one clear plan
a.why: The Whites included monarchists, officers and liberals who wanted different things. They agreed mainly on opposing the Bolsheviks, so they had no single plan. Foreign powers did help them, but that help was limited.
a.clue: Think about what held the anti-Bolshevik groups together.

b.q: Britain and Japan sent troops to Russia, yet the Reds still won. Which reason best explains this?
opts: Foreign help was limited and the Whites stayed divided
Foreign powers helped the Reds more than the Whites
Foreign troops left because the Whites had already won
Foreign powers fought each other instead of in Russia
b.why: Foreign help to the Whites was limited and could not fix their lack of unity or their wide spread. The Reds held the centre with one command. Outside help did not win the war for the Whites, so the Reds still won.
b.clue: Did outside help fix the Whites' own problems?

a.best: They were united mainly by opposition to the Bolsheviks

b.best: Foreign help was limited and the Whites stayed divided

problems.detail: "They had no single leader" overstates the case. Admiral Kolchak was proclaimed Supreme Ruler in November 1918, and Denikin formally recognised him in 1919. The standard point is that the Whites lacked effective unified command and coordination, not that no single leader existed. Safer wording: "no effective single leader or shared plan".
